K1.stone_why: A sturdy, slab-ish book face with weight and solidity, more woodcut-and-print than carved stone.
K1.carving_why: Display letters are smooth with soft bracketed wedges; no visible facets or flat-cut curves.
K1.calm_why: Even, compact rhythm and moderate contrast; the bold is heavy but never shouts.
K1.personality_why: Warm wedge serifs and condensed proportions give a friendly, distinct voice.
K1.inscription_why: Capitals are narrow and bookish, far from Roman inscriptional proportions.
K1.oblique_why: A true, consistent italic with even colour, clearly distinct from the upright and fine at 13 px.
K1.small_why: 13 px lines are sturdy and open, though the narrow set makes them a little tight.

K2.stone_why: A clean grotesque sans with no lapidary quality at all.
K2.carving_why: Perfectly smooth, engineered outlines with no cuts or facets.
K2.calm_why: Neutral and orderly, quiet though somewhat cold and technical.
K2.personality_why: Generic UI sans; competent but forgettable for this voice.
K2.inscription_why: Monoline sans capitals with no inscriptional proportion or stroke.
K2.oblique_why: Consistent, even italic clearly distinct from the upright, readable as emphasis.
K2.small_why: 13 px text is the clearest and most open of the set.

K3.stone_why: Flared, incised-looking all-caps letters evoke engraved inscriptions strongly.
K3.carving_why: Flared terminals suggest a chisel, but the curves are smooth rather than faceted.
K3.calm_why: Swashy bold caps with ligatures and unusual forms feel ornate and restless.
K3.personality_why: Very distinctive and classical, though leaning decorative and fantasy-like.
K3.inscription_why: Regular caps have true Roman inscriptional proportions; the bold swashes undercut the dignity.
K3.oblique_why: Italic small caps and swash forms are wiry and fussy, hard to read as 13 px emphasis.
K3.small_why: There is no lowercase, so 13 px running text sets in caps and small caps and reads poorly.

K4.stone_why: Rough, irregular outlines and old-style forms read as weathered, hand-cut lettering.
K4.carving_why: Display sizes show clear angular facets on the bowls and figures, like chisel cuts.
K4.calm_why: The rough edges and lively, uneven contours give a nervous, antique texture; bold barely differs from regular.
K4.personality_why: Highly memorable rustic, imperfect character that fits the Sisyphus myth.
K4.inscription_why: Capitals are classical with good proportion, though the roughness reads more weathered than formal.
K4.oblique_why: A real italic with character, but its calligraphic, bouncy forms are busy at 13 px.
K4.small_why: Readable at 13 px but the roughened edges make the text a little blotchy and uneven.

K5.stone_why: Lapidary, glyphic wedge forms with flared strokes read convincingly as cut stone.
K5.carving_why: Titles and set numbers show crisp polygonal facets and flat-cut curves throughout.
K5.calm_why: Steady rhythm and moderate weight; the faceting adds texture without aggression.
K5.personality_why: Distinct carved character that still feels refined and suits the app.
K5.inscription_why: Capitals have Roman inscriptional proportions, flared strokes and quiet dignity.
K5.oblique_why: A consistent, even italic clearly distinct from the upright and readable at 13 px.
K5.small_why: 13 px text is clean and open; the glyphic forms stay smooth at that size.

K6.stone_why: Heavy, high-contrast forms with slightly irregular edges feel solid and stony.
K6.carving_why: Display numbers and capitals show angular cuts on curves, though less crisp than a true glyphic.
K6.calm_why: Very dark and heavy overall, with an oddly hooked g, so it tends toward loud.
K6.personality_why: Strong old-style character with idiosyncratic details.
K6.inscription_why: Capitals are dignified but heavy and condensed rather than inscriptional.
K6.oblique_why: The italic is consistent but very bold and dark at 13 px, crowding the emphasis.
K6.small_why: 13 px text is dark and dense; readable but heavy compared with the others.

K7.stone_why: An elegant transitional serif, solid and classical but smooth ink rather than stone.
K7.carving_why: Curves are smooth with sharp hairline serifs; no facets at display sizes.
K7.calm_why: Even, measured rhythm and balanced contrast; very quiet with presence.
K7.personality_why: Refined and pleasant but close to a generic editorial serif.
K7.inscription_why: Well-proportioned classical capitals, though bookish rather than lapidary.
K7.oblique_why: A true italic with consistent slant, even colour and clear distinction from the upright.
K7.small_why: 13 px text is even and readable, with slightly fine hairlines.

K8.stone_why: A flared humanist sans with a hint of glyphic stroke, grounded but not carved.
K8.carving_why: Smooth flared strokes with no facets at display sizes.
K8.calm_why: Light, even and open; very calm and unhurried.
K8.personality_why: The flared stroke gives quiet distinction suited to the app.
K8.inscription_why: Capitals echo Roman proportions through flared strokes, though sans-serif.
K8.oblique_why: A clean, consistent italic distinct from the upright and readable at 13 px.
K8.small_why: 13 px text is open, even and very easy to read.

M1.stone_why: The 60 and 5 show clear facets, and the title has a firm glyphic cut.
M1.hierarchy_why: Title, set label, tracked headers, table and big numbers are distinct and orderly, with an empty middle gap.

M2.stone_why: The title and module numbers are solid and wedge-serifed but look mostly smooth at this size.
M2.hierarchy_why: Title, card labels, totals and sub-lines separate cleanly and calmly.

M3.stone_why: The History title has quiet flared serifs but little visible cutting.
M3.hierarchy_why: Title, tracked date headers, card titles and tags read as distinct roles in a calm list.

M4.stone_why: The set numbers are strongly polygonal, clearly chisel-cut, and the title matches.
M4.hierarchy_why: Roles are distinct and the rest-timer layout keeps the numbers dominant without shouting.

M5.stone_why: Faceted 60 and 5 read as cut, with a solid glyphic title.
M5.hierarchy_why: Clear title, labels, table and numbers in an orderly layout, slightly loose in the middle.

M6.stone_why: The title is grounded and glyphic but its cuts barely show at this size.
M6.hierarchy_why: The same calm, clearly layered history list with distinct roles.

M7.stone_why: The numbers are faceted but lighter and smaller, so the carving is a little less present.
M7.hierarchy_why: Tighter type sizes keep roles distinct and calm, though the big numbers carry less weight.

M8.stone_why: Lightly faceted numbers and a lighter title read as cut but understated.
M8.hierarchy_why: Orderly and calm with distinct roles; the numbers are slightly less dominant.

M9.stone_why: The This week title shows visible angular cuts on its curves, more than its twin screen.
M9.hierarchy_why: Clear separation of title, labels, totals and notes in a calm card list.

M10.stone_why: Large, strongly faceted set numbers and a cut title read clearly as carved stone.
M10.hierarchy_why: Distinct roles and a dominant number column, calm despite the timer button.
